chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I was praying in the Hijr.' A man said to me, 'Do not pray the obligatory prayer in this place, for the Hijr is part of the House.' He said, 'He spoke falsely; pray in it wherever you wish.'

key_terms.الْحِجْر: Hijr: The semi-circular walled area adjacent to the Kaaba, considered part of it in Islamic law.
key_terms.مِنَ الْبَيْتِ: Min al-Bayt: Part of the House (Kaaba), indicating inclusion in the sacred boundary.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray obligatory prayers in the Hijr of the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the Hijr al-Isma'il as an integral part of the Kaaba (Baytullah), thereby permitting the performance of obligatory prayers there despite common misconceptions. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the sanctity of the Hijr, historically associated with Ismail (AS) and the Prophet's family, grants it the same legal status as the main structure for prayer, a point of continuity with early Islamic practice.
